questions.q: The onset of central puberty is associated with increased pulsatile secretion of which hypothalamic hormone?
questions.explain: Central puberty begins when pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH secretion increases. This stimulates pituitary LH and FSH release, which activate gonadal steroid production and gametogenesis.

questions.q: A child develops pubic hair and body odour but has no breast development or testicular enlargement. Which endocrine process may explain these isolated changes?
options: Adrenarche with increased adrenal androgen production
A full activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis
questions.explain: Adrenarche is maturation of the adrenal zona reticularis with increased adrenal androgen production. It can cause pubic or axillary hair and body odour independently of gonadal puberty.

questions.q: What is puberty?
options: Period of rapid growth of the fetus before birth
Phase of declining reproductive function in later life
Transition from childhood to reproductive capability
Period of sexual differentiation in the embryo
questions.explain: Puberty is the period during which a child develops secondary sexual characters, a growth spurt and the capacity to reproduce. Sexual differentiation of the embryo happens much earlier.

open.q: What is puberty?
accept: transition from childhood to reproductive maturity

questions.q: Increased pulsatile release of which hypothalamic hormone drives the onset of puberty?
questions.explain: Increased amplitude and frequency of GnRH pulses stimulate the anterior pituitary to release LH and FSH, which activate the gonads.

open.q: Increased pulsatile release of which hypothalamic hormone drives the onset of puberty?

questions.q: What is usually the first sign of puberty in boys?
questions.explain: Testicular enlargement to a volume of about 4 mL or more is the first sign. Pubic hair, penile growth and voice change come later.

open.q: What is usually the first sign of puberty in boys?

questions.q: What is usually the first sign of puberty in girls?
questions.explain: Breast budding (thelarche) is usually the first sign, caused by ovarian estrogen. Menarche comes about 2 to 3 years later.

open.q: What is usually the first sign of puberty in girls?

questions.q: Which neuropeptide acts on GnRH neurones and is regarded as a key trigger of puberty?
questions.explain: Kisspeptin, acting through the receptor GPR54 on GnRH neurones, is essential for pubertal onset. Mutations of its receptor cause hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

open.q: Which neuropeptide acts on GnRH neurones and is regarded as a key trigger of puberty?

questions.q: Adrenarche is the increased secretion of which adrenal product?
options: DHEA and DHEAS from the zona reticularis
questions.explain: Adrenarche is the rise in adrenal androgens, mainly DHEA and DHEAS, at about 6 to 8 years. It is independent of the gonads.

open.q: Adrenarche is the increased secretion of which adrenal products?

questions.q: Which hormone mainly stimulates the growth of pubic and axillary hair in girls?
questions.explain: Girls have little testicular testosterone, so pubic and axillary hair depends on adrenal androgens. Estrogen drives breast growth, not hair growth.

open.q: Which hormones mainly stimulate the growth of pubic and axillary hair in girls?

questions.q: What defines Tanner stage 2 of breast development?
options: Projection of the areola as a secondary mound
Adult contour with only the nipple projecting
Fully mature breast with a smooth contour
Breast bud with elevation of the breast and papilla
questions.explain: Stage 2 is the breast bud stage with a small mound and enlargement of the areola. Stage 4 shows the areola as a secondary mound and stage 5 is the mature breast.

open.q: What defines Tanner stage 2 of breast development?

questions.q: About how long after the start of breast development does menarche usually occur?
questions.explain: Menarche usually occurs 2 to 3 years after thelarche, at Tanner breast stage 4.

open.q: About how long after the start of breast development does menarche usually occur?

questions.q: How does the timing of the pubertal growth spurt in girls compare with boys?
options: At the same age as boys
questions.explain: Peak height velocity occurs at about 11.5 to 12 years in girls and about 13.5 to 14 years in boys. The longer pre-pubertal growth in boys explains their greater final height.

open.q: How does the timing of the pubertal growth spurt in girls compare with boys?

questions.q: Which hormone is mainly responsible for closure of the epiphyseal growth plates at the end of puberty in both sexes?
questions.explain: Estrogen, including estrogen made from testosterone by aromatase in boys, causes the growth plates to fuse. Growth hormone promotes growth rather than closure.

open.q: Which hormone is mainly responsible for closure of the epiphyseal growth plates at the end of puberty in both sexes?

questions.q: Which testicular cells secrete testosterone under the influence of LH?
questions.explain: Leydig (interstitial) cells make testosterone in response to LH. Theca interna cells are the ovarian counterpart.

open.q: Which testicular cells secrete testosterone under the influence of LH?

questions.q: FSH acts on which testicular cells to support spermatogenesis?
questions.explain: FSH acts on Sertoli cells, which nurse the developing germ cells and secrete androgen-binding protein and inhibin.

open.q: FSH acts on which testicular cells to support spermatogenesis?
accept: Sertoli cells of the seminiferous tubules

questions.q: What is the cause of deepening of the voice in boys at puberty?
options: Hypertrophy of the pharyngeal constrictor muscles
Lengthening of the trachea and bronchi
Enlargement of the larynx with thickening of the vocal cords
Enlargement of the thyroid gland under TSH
questions.explain: Testosterone causes growth of the laryngeal cartilages and thickening and lengthening of the vocal cords, which lowers the pitch.

open.q: What is the cause of deepening of the voice in boys at puberty?
accept: growth of the larynx under androgen action

questions.q: Menstrual cycles in the first year or two after menarche are usually of what type?
options: Ovulatory with a short luteal phase
Absent FSH rise with normal ovulation
questions.explain: The positive feedback response to estrogen matures later, so early cycles are often anovulatory and irregular. Regular ovulatory cycles follow over the next 1 to 2 years.

open.q: Menstrual cycles in the first year or two after menarche are usually of what type?

questions.q: Precocious puberty in girls is defined as the appearance of secondary sexual characters before what age?
questions.explain: Development of breasts or pubic hair before 8 years in girls, or testicular enlargement before 9 years in boys, is precocious puberty.

open.q: Precocious puberty in girls is defined as the appearance of secondary sexual characters before what age?

questions.q: Delayed puberty in girls is diagnosed when there is no breast development by what age?
questions.explain: Absence of breast budding by 13 years, or no menarche by 15 to 16 years, calls for evaluation.

open.q: Delayed puberty in girls is diagnosed when there is no breast development by what age?

questions.q: A 7-year-old girl has breast development and pubic hair, an advanced bone age and a raised LH response to GnRH stimulation. What is the diagnosis?
options: Peripheral precocious puberty from an ovarian cyst
Constitutional delay of growth and puberty
questions.explain: A raised LH response to GnRH shows early activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, so this is central (GnRH-dependent) precocious puberty. Peripheral causes have suppressed gonadotropins.

open.q: A 7-year-old girl has breast development and pubic hair, an advanced bone age and a raised LH response to GnRH stimulation. What is the diagnosis?

questions.q: A 15-year-old boy has no pubertal development and cannot smell. LH, FSH and testosterone are all low. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explain: Kallmann syndrome combines anosmia with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism because GnRH neurones fail to migrate with the olfactory neurones. Klinefelter syndrome has high gonadotropins.

open.q: A 15-year-old boy has no pubertal development and cannot smell. LH, FSH and testosterone are all low. What is the diagnosis?

questions.q: A 16-year-old girl is short with a webbed neck, no breast development and primary amenorrhoea. FSH is high. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explain: Turner syndrome (45,X) causes streak ovaries, so estrogen is low and FSH and LH are high. In Mullerian agenesis, breasts develop normally.

open.q: A 16-year-old girl is short with a webbed neck, no breast development and primary amenorrhoea. FSH is high. What is the diagnosis?

questions.q: At the onset of puberty, the first rise in LH pulses occurs during which period?
questions.explain: Early puberty shows increased nocturnal, sleep-entrained LH pulses. Later in puberty the pulses are present throughout the day.

open.q: At the onset of puberty, during which period does the first rise in LH pulses occur?

questions.q: Which hormone from fat cells signals adequate energy stores and is permissive for puberty?
questions.explain: Leptin signals adequate fat stores to the hypothalamus. Very thin girls, for example athletes, can have delayed puberty and amenorrhoea.

open.q: Which hormone from fat cells signals adequate energy stores and is permissive for puberty?

questions.q: Why are gonadotropin levels low during childhood?
options: Absence of gonadotroph cells in the pituitary
Excess prolactin secretion by the pituitary
Lack of steroid receptors in the target tissues
questions.explain: The GnRH pulse generator is suppressed by central inhibition and very sensitive negative feedback. Its disinhibition triggers puberty.

open.q: Why are gonadotropin levels low during childhood?

questions.q: Which active androgen is formed from testosterone in the prostate and skin?
questions.explain: 5-alpha reductase converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone, which drives growth of the prostate, external genitalia, beard and body hair.

open.q: Which active androgen is formed from testosterone by 5-alpha reductase in the prostate and skin?

questions.q: Which pubertal change in boys is mainly due to the anabolic action of testosterone?
options: Deposition of fat over the hips
questions.explain: Testosterone increases protein synthesis, muscle mass and bone matrix. The other three changes are typical of estrogen action in girls.

open.q: Which pubertal change in boys is mainly due to the anabolic action of testosterone?

questions.q: Under the influence of estrogen at puberty, fat is deposited mainly over which areas in girls?
questions.explain: Estrogen causes the female pattern of fat distribution, mainly on the hips, thighs and breasts, together with widening of the pelvis.

open.q: Under the influence of estrogen at puberty, fat is deposited mainly over which areas in girls?

questions.q: What is the approximate average age of menarche?
questions.explain: Menarche usually occurs at about 12 to 13 years, and it is earlier with good nutrition and higher body fat.

open.q: What is the approximate average age of menarche?

questions.q: Which syndrome with café-au-lait spots and polyostotic fibrous dysplasia causes gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty?
questions.explain: An activating mutation of the Gs-alpha protein in McCune-Albright syndrome makes the ovaries autonomously secrete estrogen, so LH and FSH are suppressed.

open.q: Which syndrome with café-au-lait spots and polyostotic fibrous dysplasia causes gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty?

questions.q: Inhibin B secreted by the Sertoli cells selectively inhibits which hormone?
questions.explain: Inhibin B exerts negative feedback on pituitary FSH secretion. LH is regulated mainly by testosterone.

open.q: Inhibin B secreted by the Sertoli cells selectively inhibits which pituitary hormone?

questions.q: What is the term for the first ejaculation in a boy?
questions.explain: Spermarche is the first appearance of sperm in the ejaculate, at about 13 years. Pubarche is the first growth of pubic hair.

open.q: What is the term for the first ejaculation in a boy?
